verdict: Block's gross profit jumped 27% to $2.9B — Cash App up 38% — but restructuring charges, a large legal accrual and a $173M paper loss on its bitcoin holdings pushed it to a $309M net loss.

kpis.label: Gross profit
kpis.note: +27% YoY — the number Block steers by

kpis.label: Adjusted operating income
kpis.note: A record — a 25% margin on gross profit

segments.name: Commerce enablement
segments.note: Square's business: payment processing and tools for sellers, plus Cash App's commerce features. Square's gross payment volume grew 13% — international volume up 35% — and gross profit from this category rose 15% to about $1,608M.

segments.name: Financial solutions
segments.note: Cash App's money products — Borrow loans, Afterpay buy-now-pay-later, the Cash App Card and banking features. Gross profit jumped 55% to about $1,233M as Cash App Borrow origination volume grew 175%. Costs were just $89M against $1,322M of revenue.

segments.name: Bitcoin ecosystem
segments.note: Bitcoin bought and sold through Cash App, plus Block's bitcoin hardware and mining efforts. Revenue fell as bitcoin trading cooled and Block cut the fee it charges on some trades; $1,728M of costs against $1,796M of revenue left just $68M of gross profit, down 26%.

flow.costPlain: What Block pays to run each transaction and product: card-network fees for sellers, the cost of Cash App's money features, and the bitcoin Block buys to resell — $1,728M of the total is bitcoin cost alone.

opex.name: Product development
opex.note: Engineers and designers building Square, Cash App and Block's bitcoin products — this quarter it carries severance and other restructuring costs from the February 'Workforce Plan' reorganization.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Winning sellers for Square and new users for Cash App, including Cash App peer-to-peer processing costs.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal, people and offices. It jumped 74% because Block accrued roughly $254M more for litigation and regulatory matters, plus restructuring costs.

opex.name: Transaction & loan losses
opex.note: Money Block expects not to collect on Cash App Borrow, Afterpay and seller loans — the cost of being a lender.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of companies Block has bought.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $53M and a $173M paper loss from revaluing Block's bitcoin holdings, partly offset by $5M of other income — a net $221M cost below operating income.
footerNote: Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $308.7M.
pngFooterNote: Loss driven by one-time charges — see one-time items.
follow100Note: For every $100 of revenue, Block's products earned $48.04 of gross profit — then restructuring, legal accruals and lending losses turned the quarter into a $5.10 net loss per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Gross profit growth accelerated
takeaways.text: Gross profit rose 27% to $2,909M — Cash App contributed $1.91B (+38%) and Square $982M (+9%). Block raised its full-year gross profit guidance to $12.33B, up over 19%.

takeaways.title: Record adjusted profit
takeaways.text: Adjusted operating income hit a record $728M — a 25% margin on gross profit — and adjusted EPS rose 52% to a record $0.85. The adjusted figures strip out the quarter's restructuring and legal charges.

takeaways.title: One-time charges hid the progress
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was a $0.52 loss. A February reorganization ('Workforce Plan') loaded severance into every expense line, G&A carried roughly $254M of extra litigation and regulatory accruals, and bitcoin revaluation cost $173M — none of it from the core business slowing down.

oneTimers: A February 2026 reorganization — the 'Workforce Plan' — put severance and restructuring costs into product development, sales & marketing and G&A; management does not break out the total, but personnel costs rose sharply in all three lines.
General and administrative expense includes roughly $254M of additional accruals for litigation and regulatory matters, the main reason G&A jumped 74% year over year.
A $173M non-cash loss from revaluing Block's bitcoin holdings (a $93M loss a year ago) sits below operating income.
Adjusted figures strip out these items: adjusted operating income was a record $728M versus a $172M GAAP operating loss, and adjusted EPS was $0.85 versus -$0.52 GAAP.
